threads.thread_goal: Align on current cleaning and changeover practices and main issues.

messages.text: Kicking off the Cross-Line Hygiene and Changeover Optimization channel for the food side. For this first round, can everyone share how you currently clean and change over your food lines? Please include: 1) quick list of steps you follow now, 2) rough time each step takes, 3) where you usually get delays or need help. This will feed into T1 and the time tracking sheet in A4 so we can map the current state before we change anything.

On Line 2 I usually do: 1) stop and empty product, 2) quick scrape and sweep, 3) disassemble guards, 4) foam and rinse, 5) visual check, 6) reassemble and start. Rough times: 5 + 10 + 10 + 20 + 5 + 10 minutes. Biggest delays are when we wait for hot water or when we cannot find the right brushes. I can start logging these steps into A4 so we have a baseline for T1.

On Line 1 I just follow what we usually do: stop, push out product, sweep, then wash with hose and some chemical, then check if it looks clean and start again. I never timed each step, but I think all together it is around 45 minutes to 1 hour. I am not sure how to split the time per step for A4, maybe someone can help me fill the sheet for T1.

For Line 3, steps are similar to what was described: stop and empty, scrape, remove covers, foam, rinse, then visual check and swab if QA asks. I would say 5 min to empty, 15 min scrape and remove covers, 20 min foam and rinse, 10 min checks and reassemble. Delays: waiting for QA to release, and sometimes we share the same hose with the other line. I can start listing these steps formally for T1.

I am on Line 1 with 102838. My steps: stop, push product out, sweep floor, wipe the belt, then hose everything and put guards back. I do not always remove all covers unless there was a spill. Total time maybe 30 to 40 minutes. Sometimes we skip some details when we are in a hurry. I have not used A4 yet, but I can start writing down start and end times for each cleaning.

From the metal sawing side, for T2 we currently: 1) stop saw and lock out, 2) brush off chips from table and guards, 3) blow compressed air around blade housing, 4) shovel chips from pit, 5) wipe oil spills, 6) quick visual check around walkways. Total around 35 to 45 minutes depending on chip buildup. Delays come when chip bins are full or when we share the same broom with the other saw. I will document these steps properly for T2.

Thanks for sharing. For A4 we do not need perfect numbers at first, just rough times per step. For Line 1, could you and 527555 try this: on the next changeover, note the time when you start emptying, when you start sweeping, when you start washing, and when you restart the line. Then we can split the total into steps for T1.

Good to see the metal routine. For coordination later, it would help if we know when your chip removal usually happens so we can avoid fighting for the same forklift or walkways. Maybe we can also log your cleaning times in A4 together with ours so we see the full picture, even if T2 is focused on metal.

One issue I see often: during changeover we sometimes wait for the forklift to move pallets away from the end of the line before we can clean properly. That can add 10 to 15 minutes. Not sure if we should log that in A4 as part of cleaning time or as waiting time, but it affects downtime.

Good point on waiting for forklift. For A4, I suggest we capture both: 1) pure cleaning steps, 2) waiting or blocked time. That way for T1 and T2 we can see where the real losses are. So for each changeover, let us log: start time, end time, and any waiting periods longer than 5 minutes with a short note.

Agree on splitting active cleaning and waiting time in A4. On the saws we also lose time when we wait for maintenance to clear a jam or when chip bins are not emptied. I will start noting those separately when I fill T2 details.

For the pilot, my suggestion is we pick Line 2 on the food side. It has frequent changeovers and is not the most complex line, so we can test new steps without blocking the whole plant. On the metal side, maybe the smaller saw that already has more regular cleaning would be easier to start with.

From my side, I recommend we use Saw 2 as the pilot machine. It is easier to isolate, and we already have a bit more discipline on chip removal there. That should make it simpler to compare before and after once we start using A4 for timing.

If we use Line 2 as pilot, do we change anything on Line 1 now or wait? I just want to be sure I do not mix the new steps with the old ones before we agree. I can still help collect times for T1 on Line 1 with the current way.

For now, only the pilot line will change the sequence once we are ready. Others keep the current routine but log times in A4 so we have a baseline for T1. Based on the feedback so far, I propose: pilot food line = Line 2, pilot metal saw = Saw 2. If no one objects by tomorrow, we will lock that in and inform the supervisor.
No objection from me. Line 2 is a good choice, and I can still help on Line 3 with timing for A4 so we have comparison between lines.
All good with Saw 2 as pilot on my side. I will start mapping the current steps in more detail for T2 and prepare to log times in A4 once we start the pilot.

Closing this loop: we will use Line 2 as the pilot food line and Saw 2 as the pilot metal machine. We will capture for A4: start and end of cleaning and changeover, times per main step where possible, and any waiting periods over 5 minutes with a short note. This will complete the mapping for T1 and T2 on the pilot assets first, then we extend to the others.

threads.thread_goal: Draft and refine the new cleaning and changeover checklists.

messages.text: Sharing first drafts of the new cleaning checklists so we can refine them. For the food side, I drafted a CIP and changeover checklist for T3 that will become A1. Structure is: 1) pre-rinse and empty, 2) wash with foam and brushes, 3) rinse, 4) reassembly, 5) visual verification. For the metal sawing area, 310108 started a draft for T6 that will feed A2. Please review the structure and sequence and comment on anything missing or out of order.

On the food checklist A1, I suggest we split pre-rinse into: 1) stop and lock out, 2) remove product and open drains, 3) dry clean (scrape and sweep), 4) pre-rinse. That way T3 is clearer and we do not jump straight to water. Also, under verification, we should add a quick check for moisture in dead zones before restart.

Looking at the food checklist, I am not sure where to put the step when we remove the guards and covers. Is that in pre-rinse or in wash? In practice I remove some covers before washing and some only when I see dirt. Maybe we should write it more clearly in A1 so I know when to remove what.

Good question. I think in A1 we should say: remove all designated covers and guards right after dry clean, before foam. That way we do not forget hidden spots. Maybe we can mark which covers are mandatory every time and which are only when there was a spill, so T3 stays practical.

For me, the checklist will help because sometimes I forget the order. One thing: can we add a simple note in A1 about which chemical to use and basic safety, like gloves and goggles? I know it is obvious, but having it in T3 will remind me when I am in a rush.

On the metal checklist A2 for T6, I structured it as: 1) stop and lock out, 2) brush chips from table and guards, 3) clean blade housing and guides, 4) shovel chips from pit and empty bins, 5) wipe oil and coolant spills, 6) visual check of floor and walkways, 7) confirm guards in place. Does anyone see a need to add a step for checking around electrical panels or is that more for maintenance?

For A2 I would keep electrical panel checks as a visual only: if we see chips or dust around, we clean the outside and report anything unusual. Detailed panel checks should stay with maintenance. Maybe add a note in T6: if cover is open or damaged, call maintenance, do not touch inside.

Let us adjust A1 like this for T3: Step 1: stop and lock out. Step 2: remove product and open drains. Step 3: dry clean and remove all standard covers and guards listed for that line. Step 4: pre-rinse. Step 5: foam and brush. Step 6: rinse. Step 7: reassemble and remove lockout. Step 8: visual verification and quick moisture check. We can mark optional covers with a note. Does this sequence work for everyone?

This sequence is clear for me. Having the covers step right after dry clean in A1 will help. I just want to confirm: visual verification means checking for food residue and also for tools left inside, right?

Yes, I would say visual verification in A1 should include: no visible residue, no standing water in dead zones, no loose tools or parts, and guards correctly in place. Maybe we can add a small box in T3 to tick these four points.

I will update A2 for T6 with the note about electrical panels and also highlight critical safety zones around the blade and guards. For the sequence, I think it is fine: we always want chips and oil removed before we check walkways. I do not see any missing step for the saws we run today.

From a timing point of view, the A1 sequence you proposed should still fit within our current changeover windows on Line 2, as long as we keep the dry clean efficient. We can confirm during the pilot, but I am comfortable approving this structure for T3 so we can move on to formatting and visuals.

On my side, I am ok to lock the A2 structure for T6 as well: lock out, chip removal from table and guards, blade housing and guides, pit and bins, oil and coolant wipe, floor and walkway check, final guard check. We can still tweak wording later, but the order makes sense for safety and cleanliness.

Summing up: for A1 and T3 we will use the 8-step sequence we discussed, with clear notes on covers, chemicals, and the four-point visual check. For A2 and T6 we will use the 7-step sequence 310108 described, with critical zones and electrical panel notes. I will clean up both drafts and share formatted versions for a quick final read before we print anything.

threads.thread_goal: Define rules for shared equipment and forklift hygiene between areas.

messages.text: We need to align on forklifts and shared tools moving between food and metal zones. Right now, the same forklift can go from the sawing area to the food lines with only a quick wipe, which is risky. For T4 and A3, let us define: 1) minimum cleaning steps before a forklift enters food areas, 2) how often we log hygiene checks for shared equipment. Please share what you currently do and what would be realistic in terms of time.

From the metal side, before we go into food areas we usually just knock off visible chips from the forks and wheels with a brush. It takes 2 to 3 minutes. We do not log it anywhere. For A3 and T4, I think we should at least add: brush off chips, wipe forks with a damp cloth, and check wheels for stuck debris. Anything more complex might be hard to do during busy times.

On the food side, I often see metal dust on the forklift wheels when it comes near Line 3. Right now I just ask the driver to move slower and avoid certain areas. For A3, I would feel safer if we add a quick floor mat or tray where wheels can be rolled over after brushing, but I am not sure if we have space. At minimum, we need a clear visual check for forks and wheels before entering the food zone.

I did not know we needed a specific routine for forklifts. I usually just check if the forks look dirty. If we have A3 as a checklist, it would help me remember to look at wheels and maybe the driver seat too. I just worry that if it takes too long, drivers will skip it.

For shared tools like brooms and shovels, we sometimes bring the same broom from the metal area to sweep near the food line. There is no log. Maybe A3 should also say which tools are allowed to cross and that they must be wiped or changed before entering the food area.

To keep A3 under 5 minutes as required in T4, I suggest the minimum steps before a forklift enters food areas are: 1) brush forks and carriage, 2) inspect and brush wheels, 3) wipe forks and carriage with a designated cloth and approved cleaner, 4) quick visual check of mast and underbody for loose chips. This should be doable in 3 to 4 minutes if the station is close to the entry point.

That sequence sounds reasonable. The key for us will be having the brush and cloth right at the boundary so drivers do not have to walk far. For logging in A3, I would avoid per-movement logs; maybe a pre-shift and mid-shift check is more realistic for T4.

Agree, logging every crossing would be too heavy. For T4, I propose we log forklift hygiene checks in A3: 1) pre-shift, 2) mid-shift, and 3) whenever a forklift switches from metal to food area. The switch event could just be a quick tick and initials, not a full form.

Pre-shift and mid-shift logs make sense. For the switch event, maybe we can just have a small box in A3 where the driver marks that the cleaning was done before entering the food area. That way we do not slow them down too much.

For shared tools, could we color-code them? For example, tools that can go into food areas are one color and must follow A3 cleaning steps, and tools that stay in metal are another color. Then T4 can say that only the food-color tools are allowed to cross after cleaning.

I like the idea of a fixed station. I just want to be sure the steps are written very simply in A3, like short phrases, so drivers can see them quickly. Maybe with small icons for brush, cloth, and check.

Let us lock the minimum cleaning steps for forklifts before entering food areas as: brush forks and carriage, brush wheels, wipe forks and carriage with designated cloth and cleaner, and quick visual check of mast and underbody. This will be the standard in A3 and T4. Any objections?
No objections from me. I will talk to the other drivers so they know this will become the standard once A3 is posted.

On logging frequency, I suggest we confirm: forklift hygiene checks recorded in A3 at pre-shift and mid-shift for each forklift, plus a simple tick for each metal-to-food switch. That should satisfy T4 without adding too much paperwork.

Agreed. I will update A3 for T4 with: 1) the four-step minimum cleaning routine before entering food areas, 2) pre-shift and mid-shift full checks, 3) a quick tick box for each metal-to-food switch, and 4) a section for shared tools with color-coding guidance. Once drafted, we will test it on Line 2 and Saw 2 first.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and review pilot runs for new procedures on selected lines.

messages.text: We are ready to start pilots for the new cleaning and changeover routines on the chosen assets. Reminder: pilot food line is Line 2, pilot metal machine is Saw 2. In this thread we need to align the pilot schedule, which shifts go first, and how we will capture times in A4 for T7 and T8. Please share your shift availability and any constraints so we can confirm the plan.

On Line 2, I can cover the first pilot changeover on the morning shift tomorrow and another one the next day. That gives us at least two runs. We will need one more run on the afternoon or night shift to complete the three required for T7. I can handle the A4 timing on my runs.

For Saw 2, I can run the first updated cleaning routine on the late morning break tomorrow and another one on the same shift the following day. We usually have a natural pause then, so it should not break production. We will still need one more cycle on a different shift to close T8.
I can support one pilot run on Line 2 during the afternoon shift. I will need a quick walkthrough of the new A1 steps before we start, but I can handle the stopwatch and fill A4 for T7.

I am on Line 1 most of the time, but if needed I can join one of the Line 2 pilots to observe and help with cleaning. I am not fully confident with the new sequence yet, so I would prefer to shadow someone first.
Same here, I can help with basic tasks like dry cleaning and reassembly on Line 2 during the night shift if we schedule a pilot then. Someone else should lead the timing and checklist though.

For A4 during the pilots, let us capture: 1) start and end time of the full changeover, 2) time per main step in A1 or A2, 3) any waiting periods over 5 minutes with reason, 4) quick comments on what felt slow or confusing. This will satisfy T7 and T8 and help us adjust the sequence if needed.
Works for me. On Saw 2 I will use A2 as the step list and write the times directly into A4. I will also note if chip removal or bin emptying becomes a bottleneck under the new routine for T8.

On Line 2 I will do the same with A1 and A4. I will also check if the new cover removal step adds too much time or if it is manageable. If we see that we are close to the 2-hour limit, we will pause and inform the supervisor before continuing.
For the afternoon pilot on Line 2, I can take the lead on timing with A4 if you, 558848, can be available by chat or quick call in case I have doubts about any A1 step.
Yes, I will be available. I can also share a simple template of how I fill A4 after the first run so you can copy the approach for T7.

Putting this together, proposal for the pilot schedule: Food Line 2: 1) Morning shift tomorrow with 558848, 2) Morning shift next day with 558848, 3) Afternoon shift next day with 462838 (and 102838 observing if available). Metal Saw 2: 1) Late morning break tomorrow with 310108, 2) Late morning break next day with 310108, 3) One additional cycle on the following afternoon shift with another operator that 310108 will brief. If everyone is ok, we will confirm this as the plan.
Schedule works for me. I will align with the other Saw 2 operator for the third cycle and make sure they know how to use A2 and A4 for T8.
All good on my side. I will brief the morning team today so they know tomorrow we will follow A1 strictly and log everything in A4 for T7.
Confirmed for the afternoon pilot on Line 2. I will prepare by reviewing A1 and the previous A4 entries from the morning runs so I can compare times for T7.

Great, then we will go ahead with this schedule. First pilots on Line 2 and Saw 2 will start tomorrow morning, with morning and afternoon shifts participating first. We will review A4 data after the three runs for T7 and T8 before making any further changes.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize procedures, training briefing, and incident logging routine.

messages.text: We have completed the pilot runs on Line 2 and Saw 2 and collected times in A4. Now we need to close out the Cross-Line Hygiene and Changeover Optimization work: finalize procedures, prepare the training briefing, and agree on the incident log and handover notes. I drafted updates for A5, A6, A7, and A8, and linked them to T9, T10, and T12. Let us review pilot results and confirm what goes live for all shifts.

From the Line 2 pilots, A4 shows that the new A1 sequence added about 5 minutes on average compared to the old routine, but we had fewer re-cleans and no last-minute findings during startup. Most of the extra time came from the more systematic cover removal. Operators said the steps were clear once they got used to the order.

On Saw 2, A4 shows that cleaning time stayed about the same, but the area around the blade and walkways was consistently cleaner with the A2 sequence. The main feedback was that chip bin emptying needs to be planned better so it does not delay the routine. Overall, the new steps were easy to follow.

During the afternoon pilot on Line 2, I noticed that the visual verification step in A1 helped catch a loose tool once before restart. That alone made the extra minutes worth it. For the training briefing in A5 and T9, we should highlight this kind of example so people see the benefit.

I joined one of the pilots as observer. The new sequence in A1 was easier to follow with the checklist in front of me. For the training A5, it would help if we have pictures of each step, not just text, especially for the covers that must always be removed.

I agree on the pictures. Also, for the incident log A6 and T10, I would like it to be very simple, maybe just date, line, short description, and what we did to fix it. If it is too long, I am afraid people will not fill it during busy shifts.

The draft A6 for T10 is exactly that: date, area, issue, quick fix, and a small box to mark if it needs follow-up. It fits on half a page so we can keep it near the lines. For A8, the shift handover notes, I added a short section for hygiene status and any open cleaning issues so the next shift knows what happened.

On A5 for T9, I suggest we structure the briefing as: 1) why we changed (pilot results from A4), 2) what changed on food lines (A1), 3) what changed on metal (A2), 4) forklift and shared tools rules (A3), 5) how to use the incident log A6 and handover notes A8. We can keep it to 10 to 15 minutes if we focus on key points and examples.

That structure works for the metal team as well. For A5, I can add one or two examples from Saw 2, like how the new A2 steps reduced chips around the blade and made it easier to walk safely. That should help people see the value.

On A8, I like that we have a specific line for hygiene status. Maybe we can add simple options like: ok, needs attention next shift, or incident logged in A6. That way the incoming shift knows if they should check the log right away.

For A7 and T12, I combined the final versions of A1, A2, and A3 into one summary doc with a simple index: food lines, metal sawing, forklifts and shared tools, incident log and handover. Printed copies will go near each line and in the saw area, and a digital copy will be in the shared folder. Does anyone see anything missing before we set a go-live date?
From my side it looks complete. I just ask that during the first week after go-live we remind people at the start of the shift, maybe using A5 as a quick refresher.
For A6, will supervisors review the log weekly? It would be good to know that what we write there will be checked and not just sit on the board.
Yes, the plan in T10 is that supervisors review A6 once a week and share a short summary in this channel, using A8 notes as input. That way we close the loop on incidents and see trends.

Given the pilot results in A4 and the feedback here, I am comfortable recommending that we roll out the new procedures from A7 to all shifts starting next Monday. That gives us a few days to print A1, A2, A3, A6, A8 and run the A5 briefings for T9 and T12.
I support that date. The metal team can cover the A5 briefing in toolbox talks this week and be ready for Monday. We will also set up the A6 log and A8 handover notes near the saw area.

Then let us confirm: final procedures in A7, based on A1, A2, and A3, will go live for all shifts next Monday. A5 will be used for 10 to 15 minute briefings on each shift this week, and A6 plus A8 will start the same day as go-live. I will inform the supervisor so they can endorse the date and help with communication.
